stem: Which item is NOT included in a cash budget?

options.rationale: Correct: it is a non-cash expense.

options.content: Purchase of a delivery van for cash
options.rationale: A cash payment, so it is included.
A cash payment, so it is included.
A cash payment, so it is included.

explanation: Depreciation does not involve a payment, so it is excluded.

stem: Credit sales of US\$6,000 are made in April and customers pay one month later. In which month does the cash budget show the receipt?

options.rationale: Correct: cash arrives a month after the sale.
The sale is made in April but the cash is not yet received.
That would be two months' credit.

options.content: It is not shown, because credit sales are not cash
options.rationale: They are shown when the cash is received.

explanation: A cash budget shows cash when it moves: here in May.

stem: How is the closing bank balance for a month calculated?

options.content: Opening balance + profit for the month
options.rationale: Profit is not the same as cash flow.
The opening balance must be included.
The signs are reversed.
Correct: it is the opening balance adjusted by the net cash flow.

explanation: Closing balance = opening balance + receipts - payments.

stem: A customer pays within the month and takes a 4% discount on an invoice of US\$2,500. What amount appears as a receipt in the cash budget?

options.rationale: The discount has been ignored.
The discount has been added.
That is the discount, not the receipt.
Correct: 2,500 less 4% (US\$100).

stem: A bank loan of US\$10,000 is received in July. How is it shown in the cash budget?

options.content: As a reduction of expenses in July
options.rationale: A loan is a receipt, not a reduction of costs.
Correct: cash comes in, though it is not income.

options.content: It is excluded, because a loan is not income
options.rationale: Cash from a loan is a receipt even though it is not income.
A loan is not sales.

explanation: All cash received, including loans and capital, is shown in the month it arrives.
hints: The question is about cash, not profit.

stem: A cash budget shows an overdraft in September caused by a large dividend. Which action is MOST appropriate?

options.content: Buy extra inventory to use up the cash
options.rationale: Buying inventory worsens the shortage.

options.content: Ignore the forecast because it is only an estimate
options.rationale: Forecasts are made to be acted on.
Correct: the shortage is caused by that payment.
This increases the deficit.

explanation: Attack the cause of the shortage: delay or reduce the payment that creates it.
hints: Look at the cause of the deficit.

stem: Customers who used to pay after 30 days begin to pay after 60 days. What is the effect on the cash budget?

options.content: Profit falls by an equal amount in each of the early months of the year
options.rationale: Profit is unchanged; only the timing of cash changes.

options.content: Receipts rise in the early months because of the longer credit
options.rationale: Longer credit delays receipts.

options.content: Receipts fall in the early months and the bank balance is lower
options.rationale: Correct: cash arrives later.
Credit terms are a key input.

explanation: Longer credit delays receipts, so the early months show lower balances or overdrafts.

stem: A business can be profitable and still have a cash shortage.
explanation: True. Profit includes sales not yet collected and excludes capital spending and loan repayments.

stem: Depreciation is shown in the payments section of a cash budget because it is an expense.
explanation: False. Depreciation involves no payment, so it is left out.

stem: Match each item to its place in the cash budget.

right.content: Receipt in the month of sale

explanation: Only items that move cash are shown, in the month they move.

stem: Give one example of a non-cash item that is excluded from a cash budget.
explanation: Depreciation is the usual example.

stem: A Gweru wholesaler has sales of US\$24,000 in October and US\$30,000 in November. Half of the customers pay in the month of sale and take a 4% discount; the other half pay in the following month with no discount. Calculate the cash received from customers in November.
explanation: Prompt payers: 50% × 30,000 × 96% = 14,400. Late payers from October: 50% × 24,000 = 12,000. Total US\$26,400. Ignoring the discount gives US\$27,000.
workedSolution: 1. Prompt payers: 50% × 30,000 × 96% = 14,400. Late payers from October: 50% × 24,000 = 12,000. Total US\$26,400. Ignoring the discount gives US\$27,000.
hints: Prompt payers this month, late payers from last month.

stem: A market vendor in Harare starts May with a bank balance of US\$4,200. Budgeted receipts are US\$18,500 and budgeted payments are US\$21,700. Calculate the closing bank balance for May.
explanation: 4,200 + 18,500 - 21,700 = US\$1,000. Leaving out the opening balance gives an overdraft of US\$3,200.
workedSolution: 1. 4,200 + 18,500 - 21,700 = US\$1,000. Leaving out the opening balance gives an overdraft of US\$3,200.

stem: A Mutare hardware shop pays wages of US\$3,600, rent of US\$1,100 and drawings of US\$1,400 in September, and pays suppliers US\$9,800 for August's purchases. Depreciation for the month is US\$800. Calculate the total payments in the cash budget for September.
explanation: 3,600 + 1,100 + 1,400 + 9,800 = US\$15,900. Including depreciation (US\$16,700) would be wrong because no cash is paid.
workedSolution: 1. 3,600 + 1,100 + 1,400 + 9,800 = US\$15,900. Including depreciation (US\$16,700) would be wrong because no cash is paid.

stem: A bakery in Bulawayo has a bank balance of US\$2,500 on 1 July. The net cash flows are: July US\$3,100 inflow; August US\$4,200 outflow; September US\$2,900 outflow. Calculate the overdraft at 30 September (amount only).
explanation: July: 2,500 + 3,100 = 5,600. August: 5,600 - 4,200 = 1,400. September: 1,400 - 2,900 = -1,500, an overdraft of US\$1,500. Adding the net outflows without the opening balance gives US\$4,000.
workedSolution: 1. July: 2,500 + 3,100 = 5,600. August: 5,600 - 4,200 = 1,400. September: 1,400 - 2,900 = -1,500, an overdraft of US\$1,500. Adding the net outflows without the opening balance gives US\$4,000.
hints: Carry the balance forward month by month.

stem: A shop expects sales of US\$15,000 in a month, of which 35% are for cash. How much cash is received from sales in the month of sale?
explanation: 35% × 15,000 = US\$5,250. The rest (US\$9,750) is collected later.
workedSolution: 1. 35% × 15,000 = US\$5,250. The rest (US\$9,750) is collected later.

stem: Explain why depreciation is not included in a cash budget.

points.description: Depreciation is an accounting charge that spreads the cost of an asset over its life
No cash is paid when depreciation is recorded
The cash was paid when the asset was bought, which is shown as a payment in that month

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Depreciation spreads the cost of an asset but no cash is paid when it is charged. The cash outflow occurs when the asset is bought, so only that payment is shown.

explanation: One mark for each point.

stem: Give two ways in which a business could improve a forecast cash deficit in the next quarter and explain a drawback of each.

points.description: Delay a large payment such as a dividend, drawings or equipment
Drawback: a delay may upset suppliers, owners or staff, or postpone growth
Offer discounts for prompt payment or chase late customers
Drawback: discounts reduce income and chasing may damage customer relations

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The business could delay a large payment, but suppliers or owners may be unhappy. It could offer a discount for prompt payment, but this reduces its income.

explanation: One mark for each action and one for each drawback.
hints: Give a method and a cost for each.

stem: A business is profitable but its cash budget shows overdrafts in four months of the year. Evaluate whether the owner should be worried.

points.description: Overdrafts cost interest and the bank may refuse or withdraw the facility
The causes may be temporary (a seasonal peak, one-off equipment) rather than a permanent weakness
Profit is a good sign but cash is needed to pay bills on time
A judgement: not worried if the overdraft is short, agreed in advance and caused by timing; worried if it is rising and caused by over-trading or long credit

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Interest is a cost and the bank could withdraw the facility. If the overdrafts come from seasonal timing and are agreed in advance, the position is manageable, but if they are growing because of over-trading or slow customers the owner should act.

explanation: One mark for each point.
hints: Consider causes and the size of the shortage.

stem: Nyasha Tuck Shop in Masvingo budgets sales of US\$12,000 for March, US\$13,000 for April, US\$14,500 for May and US\$15,500 for June. 20% of sales are for cash and 80% are on credit, collected in the month after the sale. Purchases are US\$7,500 (March), US\$8,400 (April) and US\$9,100 (May), paid in the month after purchase. Expenses of US\$3,100 a month are paid in cash. Depreciation is US\$450 a month. Drawings are US\$1,200 a month. A fridge costing US\$5,500 is bought and paid for in May. The bank balance on 1 April is US\$1,800 (in credit).

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the cash received from customers in May.
parts.explanation: Cash sales 20% × 14,500 = 2,900; April credit sales 80% × 13,000 = 10,400. Total US\$13,300.
parts.workedSolution: 1. Cash sales 20% × 14,500 = 2,900; April credit sales 80% × 13,000 = 10,400. Total US\$13,300.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the total payments in May.
parts.explanation: Purchases (April) 8,400 + expenses 3,100 + drawings 1,200 + fridge 5,500 = US\$18,200. Depreciation is not a payment.
parts.workedSolution: 1. Purchases (April) 8,400 + expenses 3,100 + drawings 1,200 + fridge 5,500 = US\$18,200. Depreciation is not a payment.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Calculate the overdraft at 31 May (amount only).
parts.explanation: April closing 2,200 + May receipts 13,300 - May payments 18,200 = -2,700: an overdraft of US\$2,700.
parts.workedSolution: 1. April closing 2,200 + May receipts 13,300 - May payments 18,200 = -2,700: an overdraft of US\$2,700.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Calculate the overdraft at 30 June (amount only).
parts.explanation: June receipts 14,700 - payments 13,400 = 1,300. (2,700) + 1,300 = -1,400: an overdraft of US\$1,400.
parts.workedSolution: 1. June receipts 14,700 - payments 13,400 = 1,300. (2,700) + 1,300 = -1,400: an overdraft of US\$1,400.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Which item is left out of the cash budget?

options.content: The fridge of US\$5,500 bought in May
options.rationale: Cash is paid in May, so it is included.
Correct: no cash is paid.
Cash drawn by the owner is included.
They are included in the month paid.

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: Advise the owner on how to deal with the overdraft in May and June.

points.description: The overdraft is caused by buying the fridge for cash in May (US\$5,500)
Options: arrange an overdraft or a loan, or lease or buy the fridge on instalments
Reduce drawings or delay the fridge purchase until the balance is higher

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The overdraft arises in May because the fridge is paid for in cash. The owner could ask the bank for a short overdraft, buy the fridge on instalments, or reduce drawings for a few months.

explanation: This item prepares and interprets a cash budget for three months.

stem: A Harare stationery wholesaler has credit sales of US\$40,000 every month. At present all customers pay in the month after the sale. The owner is considering a 4% discount to customers who pay in the month of sale. She expects half of the customers to take the offer.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the cash received from customers in the month of sale under the proposal.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the monthly cost of the discount.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Evaluate whether the owner should introduce the discount.

points.description: Cash is received one month earlier from half the customers, improving the bank balance and reducing any overdraft interest
The discount costs US\$800 a month (US\$9,600 a year), which reduces profit
Compare the cost with the interest saved (4% for one month is a high price for a month's credit)
Judgement: only worthwhile if the business has a serious cash shortage or expensive borrowing; otherwise a smaller discount or chasing customers may be better

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The discount brings forward half the receipts by a month, but costs US\$800 a month. A 4% discount for one month's earlier payment is expensive compared with overdraft interest, so it is worthwhile only if cash is very short.

hints: Compare the discount cost with the benefit of earlier cash.

explanation: This item tests the effect and the cost of a cash discount.
hints: Apply the discount only to the customers who pay promptly.
